questions.title: Do the hotspot rises match burn scars?
questions.question: A hotspot is a satellite detection of heat, not a measure of burned ground. Where hotspots rose in 2026, did the burnt-area polygons rise as well?

prediction.supports: Across KHG and tenure classes, the 2026 hotspot ratio and the 2026 burn-scar ratio rank together (Spearman rho at least 0.5, p below 0.05).
prediction.rejects: The upper end of the 95% interval of rho is below 0.5: burn scars do not confirm the hotspot pattern. Not testable if fewer than 8 units lie in KHG where the 2026 burnt-area layer has at least 1 km² of scar.

method: Unit: a tenure class inside a KHG with at least 20 km² of peat in the cell panel.
Hotspot ratio: 2026 detections divided by the mean of 2015 to 2025 over the same calendar window.

Burn-scar ratio: share of the class's peat cells inside a 2026 burnt-area polygon, divided by the mean share of 2015 to 2025 (0.5 percentage points added to both, so an empty class does not divide by zero).
Spearman rank correlation of the two ratios over all units.
data: Cell panels (hotspots, burnt-area polygons BA_2015 to BA_2026 from burnt_area_2015_2026_Indonesia.gpkg)

verdict.label: inconclusive
verdict.reason: Spearman rho 0.55 (95% interval -0.12 to 0.88), p 0.10 over 10 units in the 4 KHG where the 2026 scar layer has data.

viz.title: Hotspot ratio against burn-scar ratio (2026 over 2015-2025; one dot per KHG and class; dots outside the KHG where the 2026 scar layer has data are not tested)

questions.title: Is forest area more affected than licence land or other land, in the same KHG?
questions.question: The pooled national figures mix places: forest area is mostly in Kalimantan, licences mostly in Sumatra. Within one KHG, did the forest area rise more in 2026 than the licence land and the other land next to it?

prediction.supports: The forest-area increase is above the licence-land increase and above the other-land increase, each with the interval above 1 and a ratio of at least 1.25.
prediction.rejects: The upper end of the interval is below 1.25 against both: forest area did not rise more than its neighbours.

method: Detections on peat over the same calendar window each year; counts per KHG and tenure class (tenure classes by precedence: licence, forest area without licence, other land).

Within each KHG: ratio of increases = (forest 2026 / forest 2015-2025 total) divided by (reference 2026 / reference 2015-2025 total). Exposure cancels. A KHG enters if both classes have 20 km² of peat and 10 baseline detections.
Pooled over KHG by inverse variance; the interval is the 2.5th to 97.5th percentile of a bootstrap that resamples KHG (seed fixed). Medium and high confidence together, and high alone.

The rows of single KHG use a Poisson approximation for the interval, which is too narrow when counts are large (detections of one KHG are not independent); the verdict rests on the pooled rows. Ratios beyond the axis are drawn at its end.
data: tenure_area.csv and tenure_hotspots.csv of repeat-national-tenure (34 KHG)

verdict.label: inconclusive
verdict.reason: Forest vs licence: ratio 1.18 (95% interval 0.72 to 1.65; 17 clusters, 17 strata). Forest vs other land: ratio 1.62 (95% interval 1.12 to 1.95; 20 clusters, 20 strata).

viz.title: Ratio of increases (above 1: the first class rose more than the second)

prediction.rejects: The lower end of the interval is above 0.8: no meaningful reduction. A ratio above 1 means DMPG land rose more.

method: Same ratio of increases as the previous question, with DMPG village land as the first group and land outside DMPG villages as the reference, within each KHG and tenure class (10 km² of peat in each).
Pooled over KHG and classes by inverse variance; the interval comes from a bootstrap that resamples KHG.
This tests association with the programme area, not the effect of the programme: villages were not chosen at random.

questions.title: Is forest next to licences more affected than forest far from them?
questions.question: If licence drainage pulls water out of neighbouring forest, forest within a short distance of a licence should have risen more in 2026 than forest farther away, once dome position, canal distance and road distance are held fixed.

prediction.supports: Forest within 1 km of a licence rose more than forest 3 to 10 km away: ratio of increases at least 1.25 with the interval above 1.
prediction.rejects: The upper end of the interval is below 1.25: no gradient with distance.

method: Cells: 200 m peat cells of the licence-edge run; forest area without a licence only. Distance to the nearest licence polygon of the 2025 layer (business licences used for the tenure classes).
Within strata of KHG, dome position (foot, slope, crest), canal within 500 m, road within 1 km: ratio of increases, near against far, pooled by inverse variance.
The interval resamples 5 km spatial blocks (seed fixed), so that neighbouring cells do not count as independent.
Licences are the 2025 layer applied to every year; a licence granted or withdrawn since is not represented.
data: Cell panels (licence-edge cells.csv.gz, licences, forest area, canals, roads Transportasi_Jalan_Detil.gpkg, VIIRS)

verdict.reason: ratio 0.55 (95% interval 0.42 to 0.74; 743 clusters, 46 strata): the group rose less than the reference

prediction.rejects: The upper end of the interval is below 1.25.

The canal layer maps channels, not their depth or whether they are blocked: it measures proximity, not drainage.

questions.title: Did the dome centre rise more than the dome foot?
questions.question: Water drains first from the crown of a peat dome. If water was not held there, the crest should have risen more than the foot in 2026.

prediction.supports: Forest-area crest cells rose more than foot cells: ratio at least 1.25, interval above 1.
prediction.rejects: The upper end of the interval is below 1.25.

method: Position: thirds of the KHG's peat by height above the nearest river (foot, slope, crest), from the DTM the licence-edge run chose.

Position depends on the DTM; where no river has a DTM value the run uses height above the lowest 5% of cells.

questions.title: Does the 2026 increase follow tenure boundaries or a regional pattern?
questions.question: If tenure drove the increase, blocks of forest, licence and other land should differ sharply. If a regional cause (the dry season) drove it, the increase should vary smoothly across space and cross tenure boundaries.

prediction.supports: In at least two thirds of the KHG the tenure shares of a block explain more of its 2026 increase than the mean of its eight nearest blocks.
prediction.rejects: In at least two thirds of the KHG the neighbours' mean explains more than tenure, by more than 0.05 of R²: the pattern is regional.

method: Blocks of 2 km with at least 10 peat cells. Increase per block = (2026 detections minus the 2015-2025 mean) per 100 km² of peat.
Moran's I with the 8 nearest blocks; p from 499 permutations (seed fixed).

R² of a regression of the block increase on the forest and licence shares of the block (tenure), and on the mean increase of its 8 nearest blocks (neighbours). A neighbour effect also captures any cause that is smooth in space, including tenure blocks that are large.

verdict.label: rejects
verdict.reason: Tenure explained more in 0 of 14 KHG; the neighbours explained more by over 0.05 in 13.

questions.title: Did 2026 fire return to land that had burned before?
questions.question: Fire may recur on peat already damaged and drained by earlier burns, or it may reach ground that had not burned. Were the 2026 detections concentrated on land with a burn scar from 2015 to 2025?

prediction.supports: In forest area the share of 2026 detections on previously burned land is at least 1.5 times that land's share of the area (interval lower end at or above 1.5).
prediction.rejects: The upper end of the interval is below 1.2: 2026 fire is spread over burned and unburned land alike.

method: A cell is previously burned if it lies inside a burnt-area polygon of any year 2015 to 2025 (burnt_area_2015_2026_Indonesia.gpkg).
Enrichment = (share of 2026 detections on burned cells) / (share of cells that are burned), per tenure class, pooled over all KHG in the panel.
The interval resamples 2 km blocks (seed fixed). Medium and high confidence together.

verdict.label: supports
verdict.reason: ratio 2.64 (95% interval 2.38 to 2.93; 1286 clusters, 0 strata); 62% of detections on 24% of the land. Same test in the other classes: business licence 3.42 (2.92 to 3.95); other land 4.54 (3.95 to 5.19).

questions.title: Does the 2026 fire anomaly follow the rain deficit?
questions.question: A drier 2026 would raise fire in every tenure class. Across KHG, did a larger rain deficit go with a larger hotspot increase?

prediction.supports: The 2026 rain anomaly and the hotspot ratio are negatively rank-correlated across KHG (Spearman rho at most -0.5, p below 0.05). With about a dozen KHG the interval of rho is wide, so the rule rejects only when the whole interval is above -0.5.
prediction.rejects: The lower end of the 95% interval of rho is above -0.5: a strong negative correlation is excluded.

method: Rain: CHIRPS per KHG by dekad (repeat_common.fetch_gee_balance); dekads from 1 January to the dekad starting on 21 October, every year. Anomaly = z-score of 2026 against 2018 to 2025.

Evapotranspiration is not compared: the 2026 values (MOD16 near-real-time) give anomalies of about -20 to -35 standard deviations in every KHG, which is not plausible weather and has not been explained (see repeat-neraca/docs/reports/mod16_gf_vs_nrt.md for the two MOD16 products). Left out until checked.
Hotspot ratio: 2026 detections on peat divided by the 2018-2025 mean, same calendar window; per tenure class as well.

Spearman rank correlation across the KHG of the panel. With about a dozen KHG a coefficient needs to be large to be told from chance: an inconclusive verdict means too little data to decide, not no effect.
Rain and evapotranspiration are KHG means; they do not differ between tenure classes of one KHG, so this tests the regional explanation, not the tenure contrast.

verdict.label: inconclusive
verdict.reason: Spearman rho -0.20 (95% interval -0.70 to 0.42), p 0.53 over 12 KHG. Rain in 2026 was below the 2018-2025 mean in 12 of 12 KHG (z from -3.5 to -1.1).

viz.title: Hotspot ratio against the 2026 rain anomaly (one dot per KHG)

questions.title: Was 2026 a record in forest area more often than elsewhere?
questions.question: If forest area was specially hit, 2026 should be the highest year since 2012 in forest area in more KHG than in licence land or other land. Otherwise 2026 looks like a bad year everywhere.

prediction.supports: The share of KHG in which 2026 is a record high is at least 20 percentage points higher for forest area than for the other classes (Fisher exact p below 0.05).
prediction.rejects: The difference is below 10 percentage points.

method: Unit: a tenure class in a KHG with at least 20 km² of peat and 20 detections in 2015 to 2025. Rate = detections on peat per 100 km² over 1 January to the last day of 2026 data, each year 2012 to 2026.
Record high: the 2026 rate exceeds every rate from 2012 to 2025.
Mann-Kendall trend of 2012 to 2025 (tie-corrected) for each unit, to show whether 2026 sits on a trend.
Forest units against the other units, Fisher exact test.
data: tenure_hotspots.csv and tenure_area.csv of repeat-national-tenure (34 KHG)

verdict.label: rejects
verdict.reason: 2026 is a record in 17% of 23 forest units and 16% of 51 other units (Fisher p 1.00).

questions.title: Did the forest-area season start earlier or run later than elsewhere?
questions.question: Water held back at the dome delays the start of the fire season; a deficit shifts it earlier. Was 2026's fire season in forest area shifted in time relative to licence and other land, each against its own baseline?

prediction.supports: Forest-area fire reached half of its total at least 7 days earlier (relative to its own median of 2015 to 2025) than the other classes, in the median KHG (Wilcoxon p below 0.05).
prediction.rejects: The median difference is above -3 days: no earlier shift in forest area.

method: Day of year on which half of the season's detections (1 January to the last day of data) had occurred, for forest area and for all other land, each year with at least 30 detections.
Shift = 2026 minus the median of 2015 to 2025 (at least 5 baseline years). The test is on the difference of the two shifts, over KHG with both groups.
Day of year is the calendar day of the satellite pass (UTC date).
data: Hotspot list of the cell panels (dates, tenure class)

verdict.label: not testable
verdict.reason: Only 5 KHG have 30 or more detections in the forest group and in the other group in 2026 and in at least 5 baseline years; 6 are needed.
